stem: A hospitalized client has frequent loose-stool incontinence and intact but repeatedly moist perianal skin. Which nursing intervention best helps protect the skin?

options.A: Gently cleanse after incontinence and apply a moisture-barrier product to the exposed skin
options.B: Leave stool on the skin until the next scheduled bath to minimize friction
options.C: Scrub the area vigorously after each episode to remove all residual moisture
options.D: Apply a barrier product but omit cleansing after future incontinence episodes

rationale: Open RN Nursing Fundamentals, 2nd edition, identifies prolonged moisture exposure as a skin-breakdown risk and recommends keeping skin free of excess moisture and using moisture-barrier ointments in areas subject to moisture. Barrier protection complements, rather than replaces, appropriate cleansing.
educational_objective: Use gentle cleansing and moisture-barrier protection to reduce skin injury from repeated incontinence exposure.
source_locator: Part X Integumentary > Exposure to Moisture; selected interventions to preserve skin integrity
source_claim_supported: Supports minimizing excess moisture and use of protective moisture barriers in skin exposed to incontinence/moisture.
correction_summary: Changed the item from a product-only statement to a complete nursing action that pairs cleansing with moisture-barrier protection.
audit_findings: A addresses both irritant removal and barrier protection. B and C increase skin injury risk; D falsely treats barrier cream as a substitute for cleansing.
blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Basic Care and Comfort, printed p.11 / PDF p.15
